name: Battle of the Nile

phases.title: The French line at anchor, the British closing
phases.text: The French thirteen ships of the line lay at anchor along the edge of the shoals, with the van near Aboukir Island and Orient at the centre. The British fleet came up in the evening, with Swiftsure and Alexander out of sight to the west.

phases.title: Goliath and Zealous cross the head of the line
phases.text: Foley saw a gap between Guerrier and the shoal and took Goliath through it, and Zealous followed. Orion, Theseus and Audacious also passed inside the line, which was ready to fight only on its seaward side.

phases.title: The seaward ships anchor and Culloden grounds
phases.text: Vanguard, Minotaur and Defence anchored on the seaward side of the French van, which was now caught on both sides. Bellerophon and Majestic went on to the French centre. Culloden ran onto the shoal near Aboukir Island.

phases.title: Bellerophon drifts out and the last ships join
phases.text: Bellerophon, battered by Orient, cut her anchor cables at 20:20 and drifted away from the fight. Swiftsure and Alexander came up in the dark and opened fire on Orient and Franklin.

phases.title: The French van surrenders
phases.text: Guerrier, Conquérant and Spartiate struck their colours, and Aquilon was dismasted and its officers surrendered at 21:25. Peuple Souverain had already cut its cable and drifted south, and surrendered in the night.

phases.title: Orient explodes and the centre gives way
phases.text: A fire on Orient reached her magazines at 22:00 and the ship blew up. Tonnant, Heureux and Mercure had already cut their cables and drifted south. Franklin fought on after the lull and was forced to surrender.

phases.title: The French rear stands out to sea
phases.text: Firing began again between the French southern ships and Alexander and Majestic. Heureux and Mercure had drifted onto the shoal and surrendered, Tonnant was driven ashore, and the surviving French ships stood out to sea.

note: A battle at sea, drawn as a schematic: the real line was about 2,850 yards long and the plan is not to scale. The four French frigates of the inner line, the bomb vessels and the brigs are not drawn, and the shoals are shown in the land colour. Peuple Souverain is drawn inside the French van: it cut its cable and drifted south, but the accounts do not say where it stopped, and it surrendered in the night. Leander and Timoléon are not drawn as formations: Timoléon was part of the French rear and grounded on the shoal. Swiftsure and Alexander are drawn as one block, as are the five ships that passed inside the line. The accounts do not say where Bellerophon drifted to.
